intended_object: The n-th symmetric power Symⁿ_A(X) of a module X over a commutative monoid A in a ℂ-linear symmetric monoidal category: the S_n-coinvariants (equivalently, the image of the symmetriser (1/n!)∑σ) of the relative tensor power X^{⊗_A n}. This comes from the docstring and the module (part of a formalization of Deligne's theorem on tensor categories).
explanation:
I read the definition and the ones it depends on. `modPow A X n` is the relative tensor power X^{⊗_A n}, built as a coequalizer that identifies the A-action across every pair of adjacent tensor factors. The S_n action descends to it as `modPowPerm`, and `symPowIdem` is the image of the symmetriser (1/n!)∑_σ σ under the algebra map ℂ[S_n] → End(modPow). The definition takes the coequalizer of this idempotent e with the identity. For an idempotent, coequalizer(e, id) is the splitting of e, i.e. its image; the library builds the section `symPowσ` and proves σ≫π = 𝟙 and π≫σ = e. Because 1/n! is available, the image of the symmetriser agrees with the S_n-coinvariants: a map f satisfies σ≫f = f for every σ exactly when e≫f = f. So the definition is the standard symmetric power. The degenerate cases also work: for n = 0 and n = 1 the symmetriser is the identity, so the coequalizer is the module power itself.

On generality, the construction needs n! to be invertible, so some characteristic-0 linear structure is required. The library fixes ℂ throughout (`SymGroupAlgebra n` is ℂ[S_n]), which is the ambient setting of this Deligne-theorem development. The same construction would work over any ℚ-linear category, but that is the library's base-field choice rather than something specific to this definition, so I don't count it as too narrow.

Mathlib's `SymmetricPower` covers only modules over a commutative semiring, not module objects in a monoidal category, so it is not a counterpart here.
